item.title: Morning Brief — 2026-10-16
item.description:
Good morning, Peter. Friday, October sixteenth, twenty twenty-six. The voices in this brief are AI-generated.
I'm Libby, with the weather. Spartanburg today: sunny, high around eighty-five, southwest wind two to twelve miles an hour, with gusts to twenty-one. No rain is expected today. Tonight, a slight chance of showers begins after five in the morning. Saturday will be sunny, with a high near sixty-two and north winds around ten to fourteen miles an hour.
I'm Steffan, with the Church day. The Orthodox calendar commemorates the Martyr Longinus the Centurion, along with other saints. The fasting rule is a strict fast from meat, fish, dairy, eggs, wine, and olive oil. The OCA hymn remembers Longinus confessing Christ beneath the Cross. The readings are Philippians, chapter three, and Luke, chapter nine. No feast within the next two weeks was verified in this packet.
Today's Prologue tells of Longinus, the centurion who witnessed the signs at the Crucifixion and confessed that Jesus was the Son of God. After Christ's Resurrection, Longinus refused payment to spread the claim that the disciples had stolen the body. He left Jerusalem, preached in Cappadocia, and eventually gave himself up to the soldiers sent to execute him. The hymn dwells on his confession beneath the Cross, as darkness and earthquake made the truth unmistakable. The reading also remembers a monastic Longinus, a gatekeeper at the Kiev Caves whose discernment was said to reveal the thoughts of those entering and leaving.
I'm William, with the news. In the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian villages across the northern territory on Friday, setting fire to cars and trees and beating residents during the annual olive harvest. The Associated Press reports attacks in at least eight villages, and Palestinian officials say at least four Palestinians have been killed and more than one hundred injured since the harvest began earlier this month. Israel has imposed new rules this year limiting where Palestinians may harvest, and the violence has spiked ahead of Israel's national election later this month. British officials have accused Israel of turning a blind eye to the attacks.
A teenage shooter killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday. Police say the sixteen-year-old shot his way through locked doors at Silver Rail Elementary shortly before one in the afternoon, and was then shot by a person at the scene who pursued him inside the building. The suspect was found dead minutes later. A seven-year-old child and a teacher remain hospitalized in critical condition, and Governor Tina Kotek thanked the civilian who intervened. Classes are canceled Friday across the Bend-La Pine district. On the economy, wholesale inflation jumped more than expected in September. The producer price index rose six point three percent from a year ago, the biggest increase since late twenty twenty-two, driven largely by diesel and fuel costs that are pushing up shipping and food prices. And after bipartisan backlash, President Trump said the Pentagon will no longer livestream the December firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. The plan had drawn criticism from both parties and from Catholic bishops, though the execution may still be witnessed in person by victims' families.
I'm Natasha, with South Carolina. In Simpsonville Thursday afternoon, deputies tried to stop a car, and the driver sped off instead, crashed into a home on Renwood Road, and ran. Greenville County deputies, assisted by the Spartanburg County Sheriff's Office, later detained two juveniles and charged them with possession of a stolen vehicle. No injuries were reported. In Spartanburg, police are reviewing harassment complaints after a woman on South Fairview Avenue received death threats over Halloween decorations shaped like figures wrapped in trash bags and duct tape. She took the decorations down herself and says she will not put them back up. And in politics, President Trump is scheduled to hold a midterm rally in Clemson on Wednesday, October twenty-first.
Locally, the city calendar shows a private event at Fifth Third Park in Spartanburg today, and tomorrow brings Walk A Mile in Their Shoes at Duncan Park from nine to eleven in the morning, followed by Cornerstone Baptist Church's Fall Family Fun Day from eleven to four. The forecast looks clear for both. Have a good weekend, Spartanburg.
Two verified announcements from OpenAI yesterday. The Rosalind Academic Plan offers eligible research labs up to thirty Business Standard seats at no charge for as long as twelve months, with trusted-access approval for its life-sciences model and specialized research tools. Separately, OpenAI announced a Brazilian Portuguese edition of its AI for Educators course. The company also describes Study Mode as a step-by-step learning feature that uses questions, hints, explanations, and checks for understanding. No further AI items in the supplied evidence met the verification bar.
I'm Sonia, with yesterday's recap. Gmail is available, but the packet does not identify a verified personal message that needs action. Outlook and Slack recaps are unavailable. Orders and completed or newly added Todoist items are also unavailable, so this recap may be incomplete.
Google Calendar shows no events in the supplied result; the Family and Outlook calendars are unavailable. Todoist lists overdue items for flea and tick treatment, the cell bill, measuring for the deck submission, the generator, and using the gift cards. The tomato task is due today at five p.m.; bring in the remaining full-size tomatoes before the overnight cold. Bills, packages, and order status could not be checked. Potential priority: bring in the tomatoes, then review the overdue bill and household tasks.
Looking ahead: with wholesale inflation at its highest level in nearly three years and pressure building before the November midterm elections, economists will be watching whether fuel costs keep bleeding through to grocery prices into the holiday season. That is your Morning Brief. Have a good day.
